steps.title: One connected trading lifecycle
steps.text: Hipersign ERP follows every deal from the supplier’s factory to the customer’s site. Each stage is a live count — click any of them to open the records behind it.

steps.title: Live figures for the owner
steps.text: Sales, gross and net profit, stock, receivables, cash, cheques in hand and the sales pipeline. Change the period at the top; every tile drills down.

steps.title: Your work and the top alerts
steps.text: Each person sees only what is waiting for them, plus the five most urgent alert groups — not a wall of notifications.

steps.title: Insights & alerts
steps.text: Overdue invoices, orders waiting for an advance, low stock, slow movers, thin margins, expiring visas and documents — each alert says why it matters and what to do, and opens the record.

steps.title: Trade journey
steps.text: Pick a purchase order and follow it end to end: supplier, shipment, customs, goods receipt, landed cost and the customer orders it fed.

steps.title: Messages — team, WhatsApp and email
steps.text: Team chat linked to records, plus customer WhatsApp and email in one inbox. Messages about an order sit on that order.

steps.title: One approvals inbox
steps.text: Purchase orders, discounts, credit limits, payments, credit notes, journal entries, leave and payroll — each person approves only what their role allows.

steps.title: Item master
steps.text: Brand, model and description; sales and purchase units with the conversion (1 carton = 100 Nos); weight per unit for delivery notes; warranty; minimum order; lead time and default supplier for smart reorder.

steps.title: Customer master
steps.text: Customer type, territory, billing currency, price list, sales person and website — the sales person fills in automatically on new quotations and orders. Contacts, addresses, KYC and credit sit on the same record.

steps.title: Supplier master
steps.text: Address, supplier group, lead time and website. The supplier’s lead time drives the expected arrival on new purchase orders and the reorder point of the items it supplies.

steps.title: Shared master data
steps.text: Payment terms (including advance terms), bank accounts, currencies and customer groups — add once, used by every form.

steps.title: Drop-down lists
steps.text: Every choice in a form — incoterms, ports, shipping lines, units, brands, cost centres, return and rejection reasons — is a list you own. Pick “+ Add new …” at the bottom of any drop-down to add a value without leaving the form; deactivate old values here and their history stays.

steps.title: CRM pipeline
steps.text: Leads from WhatsApp, the website and referrals move across the board; follow-ups are due-dated and a won lead becomes a customer and a quotation.

steps.title: Quotations
steps.text: Multi-line quotations with stock items, services and one-off custom items, priced from the customer’s group — sent as a bilingual PDF by email or WhatsApp.

steps.title: Price lists
steps.text: Standard Selling, Wholesale and Export (USD) — each with its own items, rates and valid-from dates. A quotation or order opens on the customer’s list and offers only that list’s items; “All products” shows everything and flags items without a list price. Changing the list re-prices the lines.

steps.title: Sales orders with credit control
steps.text: Orders above the credit limit, with deep discounts or below landed cost route for approval. Stock is reserved as soon as an order is approved.

steps.title: Price lists & pricing rules
steps.text: One standard selling list with a discount per customer group; the landed rate sits beside every price so nobody sells at a loss by accident.

steps.title: Quick, Standard or Detailed
steps.text: Every New button opens the way you like to work. Quick is a small card — customer, items and quantities, with prices, terms and validity from the defaults; type “200 cam” and press Enter. Standard shows the essential fields, Detailed every field. Switch at the top of any form without losing what you typed; the arrow changes your default.

steps.title: Sales order tracker
steps.text: Every order’s stage — stock, delivery, invoice, payment — at a glance, with the statement of account one click away.

steps.title: Customer portal
steps.text: Customers see their orders, deliveries, invoices and statement, and can pay online — fewer “where is my order?” calls. (Menu → Customer Portal opens the customer's pages as a preview.)

steps.title: Purchase requests
steps.text: Anyone can request stock; the Purchase Manager approves it and it becomes a request for quotation or a purchase order.

steps.title: Supplier quotations compared
steps.text: Send one request to several suppliers and compare price in AED, lead time and arrival date side by side — the best offer becomes the order.

steps.title: Purchase orders in the supplier’s currency
steps.text: USD, EUR or CNY orders with the exchange rate, incoterm and approval limits. A warning appears if a line is below the item’s minimum order or not a full carton.

steps.title: Smart reorder
steps.text: Sales trend, lead time and safety stock give a reorder point per item; suggestions are rounded to full cartons, respect the minimum order and go to the default supplier.

steps.title: Import shipments & customs
steps.text: ETA, bill of lading, customs documents and freight, duty and clearing charges — goods cannot be received before clearance.

steps.title: Letters of credit & trust receipts
steps.text: LC margin, documents presented, acceptance and maturity; trust receipt loans and their interest — linked to the shipment and the supplier invoice.

steps.title: Goods receiving with quality check
steps.text: Scan, accept or reject; rejected goods go to a quarantine warehouse and back to the supplier on a debit note.

steps.title: True landed cost and margin
steps.text: Freight, duty, clearing and insurance are spread over the items, so the margin on every sale is the real one.

steps.title: Stock across warehouses
steps.text: Quantity and value by warehouse and showroom, with brand and model on every line.

steps.title: Stock reservations
steps.text: Approved orders hold their stock; reservations can be released or handed to a more urgent order.

steps.title: Rack & bin locations
steps.text: Every item has a bin, so pick lists send the storekeeper straight to the shelf.

steps.title: Stock counts
steps.text: Count by warehouse or bin; differences post as a stock reconciliation after the Warehouse Manager approves.

steps.title: Serial numbers & warranty
steps.text: Look up any serial: who bought it, on which delivery and whether it is still under warranty. Claims are tracked to the end.

steps.title: Stock ageing
steps.text: How long stock has been sitting and what it is worth — slow movers also show up in Insights.

steps.title: Pick, pack & dispatch
steps.text: Pick lists, cartons and weights, delivery trips with drivers and vehicles. Orders on advance terms stay on hold until the advance is received.

steps.title: Driver app & proof of delivery
steps.text: The driver sees the day’s stops, navigates, and captures the receiver’s signature and a photo on the phone.

steps.title: Exports & re-exports
steps.text: Export orders in the customer’s currency, booked by land, sea or air with the forwarder and documents.

steps.title: Proof of export for 0% VAT
steps.text: Each shipment lists the documents the FTA needs to support zero-rating and warns before the deadline.

steps.title: Re-exports and duty refunds
steps.text: Imported goods sent out again — the customs duty paid on import is tracked for refund.

steps.title: Receivables
steps.text: Ageing by days past due and every open invoice with one-click receipt.

steps.title: Bank charges on customer transfers
steps.text: A customer pays AED 1,000 but the bank credits AED 980. On Receive payment, on the bank statement or on the invoice, the AED 20 is booked to bank charges and the invoice closes as Paid. Up to the limit anyone can absorb it; above it the Finance Manager decides — or the balance stays open.

steps.title: Customer advances
steps.text: Advances against an order or on account sit in Customer advances until they are applied to the tax invoice — automatically when the order is invoiced. VAT on an advance is reported in the month it is received.

steps.title: Payment schedule & advance before delivery
steps.text: Each order shows its instalments with what has been received and what is overdue. On 50% advance terms delivery is on hold until the advance comes in — receive it from here.

steps.title: Collections
steps.text: Reminders on WhatsApp and email by stage, with promises to pay and the customer’s history.

steps.title: Payables in any currency
steps.text: Supplier bills scanned and matched to the order. Pay a EUR or CNY bill in its own currency at the day’s rate — the realised exchange gain or loss posts by itself.

steps.title: Post-dated cheques
steps.text: Cheques in hand, due to deposit, cleared or bounced — with a maturity calendar feeding the cash forecast.

steps.title: Bank reconciliation
steps.text: Import the bank statement; lines match automatically and charges or unidentified receipts are booked in one click.

steps.title: Cash flow forecast
steps.text: Receipts and payments by due date plus operating costs give next month’s closing bank balance.

steps.title: Accounting that posts itself
steps.text: Every invoice, bill, payment, stock movement and payroll posts to the general ledger — trial balance and balance sheet are always up to date.

steps.title: Profit by branch, department and salesperson
steps.text: Cost centres split revenue and costs; head-office costs can be allocated.

steps.title: Month-end currency revaluation
steps.text: Open EUR and CNY payables and receivables are revalued at the closing rate; the unrealised gain or loss posts and reverses on the 1st. USD, OMR and SAR are pegged, so they show nil.

steps.title: Period closing
steps.text: A checklist per month — VAT, journals, payroll, invoicing, revaluation — then lock the month so nothing can be posted into it.

steps.title: UAE VAT 201 & e-invoicing
steps.text: The return builds itself from invoices, credit notes, purchase bills and advances — per emirate, with reverse charge on imports — then goes to the Finance Manager and EmaraTax.

steps.title: Corporate tax
steps.text: Accounting profit to taxable income with the adjustments, small-business relief check and the 9% charge.

steps.title: KYC & compliance
steps.text: Trade licences, TRN certificates and IDs with expiry dates; an expired licence blocks new orders until it is renewed.

steps.title: Eight companies, five countries
steps.text: The group tree: two companies in the UAE, one each in Saudi Arabia, the UK and Hong Kong, three in India — each with its own currency, ownership, head and ERPNext site. Click a country or a company to view it.

steps.title: Group, country or company — one selector
steps.text: The selector at the top switches the whole workspace between the group, a country and a single company. The group owner sees everything, converted to AED: profit at average rates, balances at closing rates.

steps.title: Country head — India only
steps.text: Vikram Rao sees the three Indian companies, India combined and their compliance — nothing from the UAE, Saudi Arabia, the UK or Hong Kong. In ERPNext this is one User Permission on the India group company.

steps.title: Company head — UK only
steps.text: James Whitfield sees only Hipersign Trading UK Ltd: its results, trial balance, journal and its own item list. Each company keeps a separate item list.

steps.title: Inter-company on both sides
steps.text: Sales to the FZE, Saudi Arabia, the UK and India and charges from the FZE and Hong Kong are booked in the other company with one click — or automatically. The reconciliation shows any difference.

steps.title: Consolidated statements & eliminations
steps.text: Investments against share capital, inter-company balances and sales, unrealised profit in stock, the minority shares in Saudi Arabia (25%) and Bengaluru (40%), and the translation reserve for the pound and the rupee.

steps.title: HR & payroll with WPS
steps.text: Attendance and leave flow into payroll, which is approved and exported as a WPS salary file.

steps.title: Expenses & advances
steps.text: Staff expense claims with receipts and recoverable VAT, settled against cash advances given to staff.

steps.title: Documents & gratuity
steps.text: Visas, Emirates IDs and labour cards with expiry alerts; end-of-service gratuity calculated under UAE labour law.

steps.title: Fixed assets & vehicles
steps.text: Register with custodian, depreciation, service and Mulkiya/insurance renewals.

steps.title: Feature packs for every size
steps.text: Starter for a small local trader, Standard for a growing importer, Enterprise for groups. Each feature can be switched on or off per company, documents can be off, recommended or fully enforced, and Simple forms hides the optional fields. Nothing is deleted — switch back and every screen returns.

steps.title: Approval rules & workflows
steps.text: Who approves what and above which amount — change a limit and it applies to the next document.

steps.title: Business rules
steps.text: Switches such as blocking receipt before customs clearance, partial deliveries, negative stock and advance before delivery.

steps.title: Document Centre
steps.text: Every record carries typed documents — the customer LPO on a sales order, the bill of lading on a shipment, the supplier invoice on a bill. This list shows each record still missing a required file, with an Attach button right in the row.

steps.title: Required documents
steps.text: For each document choose: blocks the next step, required and flagged, or optional. A blocking rule stops, for example, a supplier payment until the supplier invoice is attached — the user attaches it on the spot and carries on. Replaced files keep their older versions and every view or change is in the audit trail.

steps.title: Exceptions with approval
steps.text: When a rule blocks a step, the user can request an exception. The approver set for that rule — Sales Manager, Purchase Manager, Warehouse Manager, Finance Manager or Managing Director — allows it once, for that record. The document is still due by a date and is chased until attached. An approver can bypass on the spot, but the reason is recorded; nobody approves their own request.

steps.title: Company documents register
steps.text: Each group company’s trade licence, registrations, Ejari, civil defence, insurance policies, bank facility letters, powers of attorney and agency agreements — number, authority, expiry, owner and file. Sensitive types sit in a vault that only named roles can open.

steps.title: Compliance calendar
steps.text: One month view of everything due: licence and contract expiries, VAT, corporate tax, WPS and audit deadlines per company, plus the employee, vehicle and KYC expiries already tracked elsewhere.

steps.title: Reminders by ToDo, email and WhatsApp
steps.text: Every morning the reminder run notifies the owner at 90, 60, 30 and 7 days (set per document type) and copies the Managing Director once anything is overdue. Renewals move from Due → Submitted to the authority → Renewed, with the cost, the receipt and the new copy; the old copy is archived.

steps.title: Roles & permissions
steps.text: Each role sees only its screens; add users and switch between them from the top-right menu.

steps.title: Data migration
steps.text: Bring items, customers, suppliers, open invoices and balances across from Tally or Excel with checks before go-live.

steps.title: Test Centre
steps.text: Step-by-step user acceptance tests for every feature, by role, with pass/fail notes.

steps.title: Add-ons & pricing
steps.text: Optional modules and integrations such as WhatsApp Business, with clear pricing and implementation hours.

steps.title: See it run your business
steps.text: That’s the tour. Book a personalised demo with your own data — or keep exploring: switch users from the top-right menu, or jump to any chapter of this tour again.
